source_snapshot.message:
fix(mcp): drop launcher staleness for the CLI-listed hosts, and make --force work

A fifth review found the containment check regressed the case it was meant to
protect, and that the repair it feeds could not land on the flagship host
anyway. Both were demonstrated against the real `claude` and `codex` binaries.

**The regression.** `run()` decodes host output as UTF-8, but a Windows console
emits the OEM code page, so `where ix` returns a non-ASCII npm prefix mangled.
The row holds the real path and `expected` holds the mangled one, so a working
registration read as stale — and `install` then overwrote a config the user had
repaired by hand with a launcher that cannot start, no `--force` required. That
is the failure the previous commit said it existed to remove, reached by a
different road.

**The repair could not land.** `claude mcp add` refuses a name that already
exists and has no force flag. Seeding an isolated Claude config and running the
real `runInstall` gave `outcome: failed`, note `"MCP server ix-memory already
exists in user config"`, config unchanged — for a stale entry *and* for a
foreign one under `--force`. So `--force` was inert for Claude Code, which the
README advertises.

Staleness from a rendered listing row is therefore gone rather than fixed
again. Five attempts, five variants of the same failure: a working registration
called stale, which re-registers without `--force`. A moved npm prefix on
Claude Code, Codex and Gemini is now a manual `ix mcp install --force`. That is
a real gap, and a smaller one than silently rewriting configs that were fine.
Hosts whose config we read directly keep it: there the recorded command is
exact, and the repair is a file write that works.

`--force` is fixed independently, since it was broken for conflicts too:
`register` now takes whether it is replacing something, and hosts whose `add`
will not overwrite clear the name first. Verified against the real `claude`
binary — a foreign registration under `--force` now yields `registered` with
the entry replaced, where before it was `failed` with the entry untouched.

The launcher-shape test matrix goes with the feature it covered; the removal
argv is pinned instead, because the wiring is only observable against a host
binary CI does not have.

Six mutations caught by the intended test, 10/10 shuffle seeds clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
